quote: And yet scientists don’t torture people who question the atomic theory of chemistry. Why not?
content: Lysenkoism supports the essay. Its criterion was conformity to dialectical materialism and to "Michurinist" doctrine, which is a criterion of comparison. Lysenko's results were not replicated. When experiment and doctrine collided, doctrine won by decree at the 1948 VASKhNIL session, and the geneticists were then removed. That is what the essay predicts once the experimental "criterion of goodness" is replaced by authority: "The bigger guns win." American eugenic sterilization was defended in the language of preventing decline: "Three generations of imbeciles are enough" (Buck v. Bell, 1927). The Inquisition's caution about witches is real, but its business was heresy, where the criterion was conformity to doctrine. Scientists have held coercive power over careers, and the essay notes that stagnant fields use it.

quote: Nearly all cultures before the Enlightenment believed in a Fall from Grace—that things had once been perfect in the distant past
content: Fable's own counterexamples show which view dominated. Augustine's linear history runs from a perfect Eden through the Fall, and restoration comes at the end, from God, not from human improvement. That is the Fall-from-Grace scheme with an arrow drawn on it. Joachim of Fiore, the one medieval thinker with a truly progressive scheme of ages, had his Trinitarian doctrine condemned by the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215, and his followers' teaching was condemned again in the 1250s and 1260s. Condemning the future-facing view as heresy is what the essay says guardians do. Lucretius was an Epicurean, a minority school. On "turn mean": when a star scientist dies, outsiders' work in the field rises significantly, which means incumbents had been keeping them out (Azoulay, Fons-Rosen & Graff Zivin 2019).
